title: Station alarm
text: An alarm screams through the station at 3 a.m. A coolant line is leaking and mission control's instructions are garbled.

choices.label: Fix it yourself by the book

outcomes.text: I traced the leak, sealed it and went back to sleep. Mission control called it textbook.
The patch held, but I inhaled fumes and spent a week in the medical bay.
Duct tape and a sock. It worked. The internet made me a meme.
The tape failed. We had to abort the experiment and come home early.
The commander fixed it and quietly wrote me up for hesitating.
The commander was already awake, staring at the same gauge. We fixed it together and never spoke of the delay.

title: Spacewalk
text: You're scheduled for your first spacewalk. Your heart rate is already at 130.

choices.label: Go out and do the job

outcomes.text: I floated above the Earth for six hours. I cried inside my helmet. Nobody could see.
My tether snagged and I drifted for 40 terrifying seconds before it caught.

choices.label: Ask for a sim run first

outcomes.text: The extra practice paid off. The spacewalk went perfectly.
The sim showed a flaw in my suit checklist that nobody had caught. Mission control thanked me in public.
The delay cost us a launch window. The mission was rescheduled and my name was in every meeting.

choices.label: Ask for a veteran to accompany you

outcomes.text: A veteran came with me and talked me through every move. I'll never forget the voice.
The veteran was ill, and I spent three days waiting for a replacement who barely spoke.

title: Close quarters
text: Six months in a tin can with {c.first}. Things have gotten... cozy.

outcomes.text: I started a relationship in orbit. Mission control pretended not to notice.
{c.first} was not interested. The next four months were very awkward.
I kept it professional. We're still good friends.
A month after landing, {c.first} wrote me a letter. I kept it unopened for a year.
The mission succeeded in part because nothing else was on our minds. We didn't talk afterward.

choices.label: Talk about it openly with the commander

outcomes.text: The commander was relaxed about it, and asked only for discretion. We were both embarrassed and relieved.
The commander said no, politely, and added a note to my file.

title: Selection board
text: The agency asks you to recommend a candidate for the next astronaut class. {f.first} would kill for this.

outcomes.text: {f.first} was selected. {f.He} hugged me so hard I felt it in my ribs.
{f.first} washed out of training and blamed me for getting {f.his} hopes up.
I recommended a stranger with a better record. {f.first} found out.
{f.first} made it on their own the following year. They never mentioned my recommendation and neither did I.
The stranger washed out in training. {f.first} would have passed. I'll carry that.
I wrote both honestly. The agency took the stronger candidate and thanked me for the clarity.
I wrote both and the agency chose neither, citing 'concerns about balance'.

title: Space rock
text: A collector offers to buy a sliver of moon rock you 'accidentally' brought home.

outcomes.text: I sold it for $80,000. Then the agency's inventory audit came around.
The collector was a federal agent. I was charged with theft of government property.
I returned it. The agency never knew it was gone.
The collector raised his price each time I declined, which made it harder. I still said no.
The agency noticed. It cost me a promotion, but I couldn't have lived with the alternative.

choices.label: Donate it anonymously to a museum

outcomes.text: It went on display in a small museum with a plaque 'donor wishes to remain unknown.' I visit it sometimes.
The museum authenticated it and traced it to a mission. There was an inquiry, and I was not anonymous for long.

title: Launch day
text: Your family is at the viewing stands for your launch.

outcomes.text: I waved from the gantry. {m.first} said it was the proudest day of {m.his} life.
{m.first} wept so hard that the cameras picked it up. It became the image of the launch.
I couldn't see {m.first} from the gantry. I waved at a crowd and hoped.

choices.label: Record a message for them to watch afterwards

outcomes.text: I recorded two minutes in a spacesuit. My mother has watched it more times than she'd admit.
The message was cut by the agency for 'technical reasons'. I felt oddly crushed.

choices.label: Look for them and mouth a thank-you

outcomes.text: I found them in the crowd. My father held up a sign that said 'WE SEE YOU'. I did not cry until the gantry door closed.
I couldn't find them in the crowd. I thanked the whole stand instead, and the camera caught it.

choices.label: Keep your focus on the checklist

outcomes.text: The launch went flawlessly and I never looked once. My mother said she understood. She didn't, entirely.
I kept my focus. A minor valve fault was caught because of it.

title: Memoir offer
text: A publisher wants the book of your life in orbit.

outcomes.text: "The View From Up There" became a bestseller.
The book was honest, slow and sold modestly.
The ghostwriter made me sound like an action hero. It sold well.
The ghostwriter got a detail wrong, and a retired colonel wrote to the publisher. The second printing has a correction.
We argued for months. The finished book was less heroic and more honest, and I like it better.
It took a year of long interviews. The book was richer than either of us would have written alone.
The journalist and I fell out over a chapter. The book came out anyway, with two differing prefaces.

title: Size zero
text: Your agency says you need to lose weight for the fall shows.

choices.label: Refuse and speak up about it

outcomes.text: My post about it went viral. Other models thanked me.
The agency dropped me for being 'difficult'.
I found an agency that books me as I am.
The new agency paid less and treated me like a person. I stayed for six years.
Word got around that I was difficult. The new agency dropped me after two shoots.
I worked with a nutritionist and got stronger, not smaller.
The coach became a close friend. The agency eventually admitted I looked better.
Progress was slow and the fall shows went by without me. The spring ones didn't.

title: Creepy photographer
text: A famous photographer keeps making inappropriate comments during a shoot.

outcomes.text: I walked out. Three other models followed me.
The photographer's agency blacklisted me for a year. So did his friends. I slept well.
My agency backed me and he was dropped by two brands. It was in the trade press for a week.
I went public. He was dropped by every magazine.
Nobody believed me at first. It cost me bookings for a year.
I finished the shoot and felt awful about it.
Months later the photographer was exposed in a long report. I was quoted as "no comment" and lay awake that night.
The photos were the best of my career. I hate that.

title: Your own line
text: A fast-fashion giant wants to launch a collection with your name on it.

outcomes.text: The collection sold out in an hour. I made $600,000.
The clothes fell apart after one wash. Fans were furious.
I turned them down and started planning my own fashion label.
The label took two years to break even, and I nearly lost my home. But it was mine.
A department store picked up my first line. The fast-fashion giant copied it a season later.
They agreed to a capsule collection with my input. It sold out in a weekend.
They said no, and signed someone else the same day.

title: Runway rival
text: {r.first}, a rival model, 'accidentally' spilled coffee on your outfit before the show.

outcomes.text: I walked in the stained outfit like it was on purpose. It became the look of the season.
The coffee smell followed me down the catwalk. A critic called it "a metaphor I'm still unpacking."
I tripped halfway. Nobody forgot.
I switched {r.first}'s shoes for a size smaller. {r.He} stumbled on the runway.
{r.first} got hurt. I never meant for that. I sent flowers anonymously.
It worked. {r.first} vanished from the circuit. The win tasted like pennies.
The designer cut {r.first} from the show.
The designer laughed and said it happens to everyone. I lost a day of goodwill.
{r.first} was replaced by a newcomer, who turned out to be better than both of us.

title: Scout
text: A scout at your agency spots {f.first} in your photos and wants {f.him} too.

outcomes.text: {f.first} signed with the agency. We did our first shoot together.
{f.first} outshone me at the first casting and got the job I wanted. We haven't spoken since.
{f.first} hated the industry within a month but thanked me for trying it.
I kept my spotlight to myself. {f.first} never found out.
{f.first} found out from the scout. Their silence was louder than any argument.

choices.label: Introduce them but stay out of it

outcomes.text: I made the introduction and left the room. They got a good offer. We're closer than before.
I made the introduction and they got a better offer than mine. Friendship survived, with a long silence in the middle.

title: New faces
text: The agency is sending all the good bookings to 19-year-olds.

outcomes.text: I started taking acting classes. The camera already loves me.
The acting classes were humbling. The camera loves me, but the script has other ideas.
A small role in an indie film led to a bigger one. The industry has room for me.
I moved behind the scenes and started scouting.
The first model I signed became the face of a campaign and credited me in an interview.
Booking meant a different kind of cruelty: telling nineteen-year-olds they weren't quite right. I hated it.
I kept taking every job I could get.
A tabloid ran my age on the front page. I kept working through the week.
A heritage brand hired me to play a "timeless" woman. The campaign ran for years.

title: Weight cut
text: You're four pounds over with 24 hours until weigh-ins.

outcomes.text: I made weight but felt like a ghost in the cage.
I collapsed in the sauna and was rushed to the hospital.

choices.label: Miss weight and pay the fine

outcomes.text: I paid a 20% fine and fought at full strength.
I missed weight and my opponent refused the bout. The fine was the smaller loss.
The extra four pounds made the difference and I won by knockout. The fine felt cheap.

choices.label: Cut weight gradually, and carry the risk

outcomes.text: Three more hours of careful dieting. I made weight with ounces to spare and felt fine.
Gradual wasn't enough. I missed by half a pound and the commission gave me an hour.

title: Callout
text: After your last win, you grab the mic. The crowd is roaring.

outcomes.text: The clip got 20 million views. The champion accepted.
The champion laughed it off. I looked desperate.
I thanked my mom on live TV. Everyone loved it.
My mother watched it live and called me in tears. It was the best call of my career.
I forgot my sister's name. She posted about it. We argued for a week.

choices.label: Stay quiet and let the performance speak

outcomes.text: The silence was more powerful than any speech. The champion's camp called the next morning.
The silence made me look dull. The promoter was annoyed.

title: Street challenge
text: A guy at a bar recognizes you and wants to prove he can take you.

choices.label: Fight him in the parking lot

outcomes.text: I walked away. Professionals don't fight for free.
Someone filmed me walking away. The clip was shared with a caption I wouldn't repeat.
The man apologised the next morning at my gym and asked for a lesson.

choices.label: Sign him to a sparring session

outcomes.text: I told him to come to my gym. He lasted 40 seconds.
He came in cocky and went out with a broken nose. He also signed up for membership.
He never showed. I heard later he lied about the whole thing.

title: Doctor's warning
text: After your last fight, a neurologist wants to talk about the long-term damage.

outcomes.text: I retired while I could still remember my wins.
Retirement was harder than I expected. I woke up every day with nothing to train for.
I retired and set up a clinic for old fighters. The neurologist became my partner.
I kept fighting. My hands shake a little in the mornings now.
The next fight was my best. The one after that I can't remember at all.
I lost the belt and my memory of how. I smile when people tell me about it.
The second neurologist agreed with the first, more gently. I took the advice more seriously for being given it twice.
The second neurologist gave a more hopeful read. I wanted to believe it.

title: Corner
text: {f.first} offers to be your cornerman for the next fight.

outcomes.text: {f.first} was a natural in the corner. We won the next fight together.
{f.first} threw in the towel too early. We argued for weeks.
I kept my old coach. {f.first} understood.
My coach stopped coaching a month later. {f.first} had already moved on to another fighter.
My coach spotted a flaw in my opponent that {f.first} would never have seen. I won.
I used both. They disagreed constantly, and I won because of the argument.
Having both was chaos. I lost the first round trying to listen to two voices.

title: Your own gym
text: An investor wants to open a gym chain with your name on the door.

outcomes.text: I put my name on a line of gyms. The first one opened to a line around the block.
outcomes.milestone: lent their name to a gym chain

outcomes.text: The business partner overextended and the chain folded. My name was still on the door.
The gym chain grew faster than I could keep up. I became a spokesperson and a happy millionaire.
I stayed focused. The belt comes first.
The investor signed someone else. A year later I lost my title and wondered.
I won the belt that year. I opened a gym later with no partners and no debts.

choices.label: Take a smaller stake, keep control

outcomes.text: A small gym with my name over the door and a team I picked. It was modest and happy.
The investor insisted on a bigger stake. We parted on awkward terms.

title: Diva on set
text: Your lead actor is refusing to leave their trailer until the script is rewritten.

outcomes.text: The rewrite was actually better. The movie improved.
The rewrite took until 3 a.m. and the actor and I became friends for life.
The actor's rewrite was worse. We filmed it anyway and I regret it.
They came out in five minutes flat.
They quit. Reshoots cost $2 million.

choices.label: Film the tantrum for the blooper reel

outcomes.text: The blooper reel went viral before the movie came out.
The actor saw the reel, didn't find it funny, and sued. I lost a week to lawyers.
The studio loved the reel. The actor, to my relief, did too.

title: Studio notes
text: The studio wants a happier ending. Test audiences cried too much.

outcomes.text: I won the fight. Critics called it brave.
The studio took the movie away from me and recut it.
I gave them the happy ending. It made more money and meant less.
Audiences loved it and critics called it "a betrayal". I've never decided if they were wrong.
The happy ending tested poorly, to the studio's surprise. They blamed me.
A quiet scene I added to the ending became the one everybody remembers.
I shot both. The studio chose the happy one, then a festival chose mine. The director's cut was legendary.
I shot both. The studio chose the happy one and buried mine.

title: Nepotism
text: {k.first} wants a part in your next movie. {k.He} has never acted.

outcomes.text: {k.first} was a revelation. The critics loved {k.him}.
{k.first} was wooden and the reviews said so. By name.
{k.first} got one line. {k.He} practiced it for a month.
{k.first} froze on camera. We shot forty takes. The final cut used the first one.
{k.first} was so good that a casting director asked for their number.

choices.label: Hire them as an assistant on set

outcomes.text: They loved it. They fetched coffee and watched the entire shoot, and a career began.
They hated the early starts and left after a week. We laughed about it.

title: Film festival
text: Your movie was selected for a big European film festival.

outcomes.text: A ten-minute standing ovation. I have never felt anything like it.
People walked out. One critic booed.
I stayed home and started my next script.
The film won a prize at the festival in my absence. The prize was accepted by someone in my seat.
The script I wrote that week became my best. I wouldn't trade it.
The video was warmly received and widely shared. I got to work that night.
The video message froze on a bad frame and became a meme for a week.

title: Stunt gone wrong
text: A stunt performer was hurt on your set. The union is investigating.

outcomes.text: I paid for everything and changed our safety rules. The union respected it.
The stunt performer recovered and thanked me in person. The safety rules I wrote became an industry standard.
The insurance didn't cover it, and the studio walked. I sold my car and my reputation held.
The coordinator was fired. The crew didn't forget.
The coordinator sued for wrongful termination and won. So did the union.
{lw.first} handled everything quietly.
The lawyer advised me to say nothing. I said nothing, for as long as I could.

title: Studio offer
text: A studio wants to buy your production company, or back you in building your own.

outcomes.text: I'll build my own studio. Look for it under Occupation → Business.
The studio nearly bankrupted me in year one. By year three it was a name in the industry.
I signed an overall deal worth $2 million.
The studio controlled every cut. I made three films I'm not proud of, and I'm wealthy.
The deal made my next film possible, and the film won. I called it a good trade.

choices.label: Ask for a producing deal and keep your company

outcomes.text: A middle path: they financed three films, and I kept the company. It was a compromise that worked.
They declined the middle path and offered the bigger deal again.

title: Honeytrap
text: A charming stranger at the embassy party is asking a lot of questions about your 'insurance work'.

outcomes.text: By dawn, they were working for us.
They turned, but only for a month. Then I found their name on a list that wasn't mine.
I never found out who they really worked for. That bothers me more than it should.
I slipped out the kitchen door. Better safe.
I later learned it was a test from HQ. I passed.
The stranger was a real threat and I was followed for three blocks. I lost them in a market.
I said too much. HQ pulled me in for a very long conversation.
HQ gave me a second chance and a babysitter. I am not allowed to forget it.

title: Cover story
text: {f.first} saw you in a city you weren't supposed to be in.

outcomes.text: {f.first} bought it. I felt terrible.
{f.first} didn't believe me. Things are different between us now.
I told {f.first}. HQ found out.
{f.first} kept the secret for forty years and never once brought it up. That was the gift.
{f.first} left and told nobody. I stopped hearing from them.
HQ never found out. {f.first} looked at me for a long time and asked if I was okay.

choices.label: Say it was a surprise party, and plan one

outcomes.text: I really planned one. It was lovely. And the cover held, for the moment.
The excuse was believed, but I had to plan a party I couldn't afford.

title: The mole
text: Someone in your unit is selling secrets. All the evidence points to {c.first}, your closest colleague.

outcomes.text: {c.first} was the mole. I was promoted.
{c.first} was innocent. The real mole framed {c.him}.
{c.first} vanished the next day. So did the evidence.
{c.first} was innocent. The real mole left the next week. I should have looked harder.
{c.first} turned themselves in and cleared their name. They never forgave my doubt.

title: Burn notice
text: HQ has disavowed you. Your accounts are frozen and your cover is useless.

outcomes.text: I spent a year proving my innocence. I got my job back and a medal.
I couldn't clear it. I left the service for good.
I disappeared. New name, new country, new life.
I built a new life in a coastal town. After a year a stranger recognised me in a pharmacy.
Nothing followed me, which was somehow worse. I spent a year waiting for a knock.

choices.label: Contact an old friend inside the service

outcomes.text: A friend I trusted passed me a file. It cleared part of my name.
The friend was watched, and I'd made it worse for both of us.

title: Old friends
text: Two men from your old crime family are waiting outside your house. They know you were the informant.

outcomes.text: A black van arrived in four minutes. I never saw those men again.
My handler didn't answer. I barely escaped.
I left that night with one suitcase.
I got out. A cousin told me the men were still waiting at my door six months later.
My flight was delayed and I spent six hours looking at every face in the terminal. Nobody came.

title: Quiet life
text: After years of lies, you just want to garden and see your family.

outcomes.text: I retired with a pension and a medal I can never show anyone.
The garden died in the first frost. I have bought another.
Two weeks in, a former colleague called to say I was needed again. I said no, and the phone kept ringing.
One last mission. They always say that.
The last mission was easier than it should have been. That frightened me more.
I retired after that. A medal in a drawer and no one to tell.
A desk role with a window and a pension. I told myself it was a compromise and found I enjoyed it.
The desk role was dull enough to be dangerous. I started looking for excitement elsewhere.
